title: I Ended the Retail Standoff by Selling Her the Broken Display

parts.text: I sold her the smashed display candle because she demanded the display price. I am twenty-four, cashier, cinnamon everywhere, holiday hell. Denise wanted the intact candle at the damaged price. Craig said honor the customer. The sign on the display said DISPLAY NOT FOR SALE, then in marker, DAMAGED $4. She pointed at $4. I pointed at smashed wax on the tray, a specific purple puddle. I rang the smashed one for $4. She blinked. She did not want smashed. She wanted intact at smashed. I followed the sign. Craig tried to override. The line behind her started a slow clap I did not ask for, embarrassing, effective. She left. I boxed the puddle for hazardous-ish trash. My hands smelled like lavender violence. I still think display signs should be treated like spells: exact words, no vibes. Denise said, "I want that one for four dollars" I said, "That one is the puddle. The puddle is four" A kid said it was like a video game. It was not. It was retail. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink.
